mike_r: quick heads-up from today's continuous-batching probe on corp-qa — we saw a pronounced decode-rate slope that causes lots of tiny batches for mid-length prompts, and that coincides with KV churn spikes. attaching notes and a short log snippet.

bench-bot: probe finished: mk-lsx kernel p99 latency +18% vs baseline, overall throughput -6%. data at /bench/probes/3345001234.

jia: can you paste the minimal repro (config + short traces)? curious whether it's admission logic or kernel switch frequency. :thinking:

mike_r: repro + sample: 
```
# seq distribution sample (N=10k)
median_seq=48
p75_seq=130
p90_seq=310
observed_decode_slope ~= 0.72  # tokens/sec growth vs prompt len
\n# config used
token_budget_target=64
max_batch_size=64
admission_window_ms=120
cohort_classifier=prompt_len_buckets: [0-32,33-128,129-512]
kernel_policy: prefer mk-lsx, fallback fp16-mk
```
Result: lots of requests in 129-512 bucket getting admitted with token_budget 64 -> decode stage quickly evicts KV entries, kernel keeps flipping to fp16 fallback briefly, then back. net: small microbatches + KV thrash.

anya: that token_budget_target=64 feels low for a p90~310. Those requests will decode for ~5-6x the budget. Suggest trying token_budget_target=128 and increasing admission_window to 200-250ms to allow better batch accrual.

sam: also check the cohort classifier boundaries — the 33-128 bucket is catching many midlen tails. Maybe split into [33-96,97-256] so kernel selection has clearer signal. Could reduce kernel flips.

jia: agreed. quick experiment plan: 1) token_budget_target=128 2) admission_window_ms=220 3) bucket split 33-96/97-256 4) enable kv-prefetch=true on the mk-lsx path. I'll run a 1h probe.

bench-bot: new run queued with id 3345001245 (params above). ETA 65m.

mike_r: thanks. if that reduces p99 to <+5% and throughput loss <2%, we can consider rolling this into the canary for dedicated pools. Also we should add a short histogram of kernel handoff counts per request to the probe output.

sam: note — when kv-prefetch=true we saw slightly higher memory pressure on smaller GPU instances. add a safeguard: kv-prefetch only when free_kv_slots >= 0.25.

jia: ack. I'll add that in the probe config. running now, will post results and a short diff of the admission logic.

anya: one more thing — add a tiny eval set of prompts that exercise long-context decode ramp (50-300 tokens) so we can track quality regression after quant/kernel changes.

mike_r: good call. tagging this thread for follow-up after bench results. @bench-bot please post summary table (p50/p90/p99, kernel-handoffs, kv-evictions) when done. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: probe complete: 3345001245 summary -> p99 +3.8%, throughput -1.6%, kernel-handoff median 0.9/request, kv-evictions down 42% vs baseline. Full CSV uploaded to /bench/results/3345001245.csv

mike_r: that's promising. can we run a short 30m stress at 5x qps to validate no regression under load before scheduling canary?

jia: will queue stress run under same config and report back.

anya: thanks team — looks like classifier granularity + bumped token budget helped the batching formation and reduced KV churn. follow-ups: add kernel-handoff histogram to runtime tracing and consider making the 33-96/97-256 split a dynamic config driven by observed p90.
